findings.highlight: I don’t want to just sit here doing nothing.
findings.evidenceJa: こうして何もしないというのも所在がない
findings.governingReading: Remaining motionless with nothing to do leaves Shirou awkward, restless, and unsure of himself.
findings.explanation: The English turns an involuntary sense of unease into a simple preference against inactivity.

findings.highlight: still meditating
findings.evidenceJa: 座禅を組んだまま
findings.governingReading: still seated in a cross-legged Zen posture
findings.explanation: Meditating adds a mental practice where the source specifies only Shirou’s seated posture during the circuit examination.

findings.highlight: she never did anything because she wanted to
findings.evidenceJa: あいつが自分から何かやるって今までなかった
findings.governingReading: Until now, Saber has never initiated an action on her own.
findings.explanation: The English changes lack of self-initiated action into never acting from personal desire, prematurely interpreting the very issue Shirou is trying to formulate.

findings.highlight: she’s so unselfish
findings.evidenceJa: あんまりにも無欲すぎる
findings.governingReading: she is far too devoid of personal desire
findings.explanation: Unselfish gives Saber a positive moral trait; 無欲 describes the unsettling absence of wants that Shirou does not know how to address.

findings.highlight: make up for her sad end
findings.evidenceJa: あいつの最期に報いる
findings.governingReading: do something worthy of, or in recompense for, how Saber met her end
findings.explanation: Make up for treats Saber’s death like a correctable deficit and adds “sad,” while Shirou is thinking of repaying or honoring it.

findings.highlight: Saber has to fight for her own wishes
findings.evidenceJa: 何より自分の望みの為に戦わなくちゃいけない
findings.governingReading: Above all else, Saber must fight for her own wish.
findings.explanation: The English removes Shirou’s emphatic ranking of Saber’s own wish above every other reason and changes the singular wish to plural.

findings.highlight: must have been shocked
findings.evidenceJa: 呆れたのか
findings.governingReading: perhaps exasperated or dumbfounded by his behavior
findings.explanation: Shock supplies the wrong reaction and “must” promotes Shirou’s tentative reading into certainty.

findings.highlight: I distorted her personality for a moment.
findings.evidenceJa: 彼女の姿を、ねじ曲げた
findings.governingReading: For one instant, Shirou twisted his image or conception of who Saber was.
findings.explanation: Personality narrows Shirou’s admission: he distorted the figure of Saber before him to fit what he wanted to believe.

findings.highlight: said the same things as you
findings.evidenceJa: 似たような事を言ってた
findings.governingReading: said something similar to what Shirou had said
findings.explanation: Same overstates the parallel between Archer’s world-peace answer and Shirou’s claim about Saber’s self-directed wish.

findings.highlight: he made no effort to talk to me or Saber
findings.evidenceJa: 努めて俺やセイバーとは接触しなかった
findings.governingReading: Archer deliberately made a point of avoiding contact with Shirou and Saber.
findings.explanation: The English reverses intentional restraint into a mere failure to make conversational effort and narrows contact to talking.

findings.highlight: but  I know  he wouldn’t have a stupid objective
findings.evidenceJa: 馬鹿げた目的を持つヤツじゃなかった
findings.governingReading: He was not the sort of man to pursue a ridiculous objective.
findings.explanation: The active English contains an exposed insertion candidate with doubled spaces, interrupting Shirou’s assessment.

findings.highlight: world peace
findings.evidenceJa: 恒久的な世界平和
findings.governingReading: permanent or everlasting world peace
findings.explanation: The English omits permanence from Archer’s proposed wish, weakening the absolute condition Rin attacks on the next page.

findings.highlight: he got timid
findings.evidenceJa: いじけちゃってさ
findings.governingReading: Rin says Archer sulked or became petulant after she laughed.
findings.explanation: Timid changes Rin’s teasing characterization of wounded, sulky pride into fearfulness.

findings.highlight: got summoned by someone like me
findings.evidenceJa: わたしみたいな小娘に使役されちゃう
findings.governingReading: ended up being made to serve a little girl like Rin
findings.explanation: Another use of 使役 is neutralized into summoning, erasing Rin’s joke about Archer’s grand manner ending in subordination to her.

findings.highlight: I am still chasing a foolish dream
findings.evidenceJa: 愚者の夢を守っている
findings.governingReading: Even now, in this one respect, I continue to protect the fool’s dream.
findings.explanation: Chasing makes Archer personally pursue the ideal, while the source says he preserves or defends it despite sharing the wise critique.

findings.highlight: He was so snobbish, right?
findings.evidenceJa: キザでしょ？
findings.governingReading: Affectedly suave or theatrical, wasn’t he?
findings.explanation: Snobbish assigns class condescension; Rin is teasing Archer’s self-consciously stylish gallantry in yielding his wish to her.

findings.highlight: I’ve had it forced upon me
findings.evidenceJa: 嫌でも思い知らされている
findings.governingReading: He has been made acutely aware of it these last few days, whether he liked it or not.
findings.explanation: The English suggests the legend itself was imposed on Shirou, losing the sense that experience with Saber has forced him to recognize its reality.

findings.highlight: He was a crossbreed with an Incubus
findings.evidenceJa: 悪魔じみたヤツ
findings.governingReading: a demon-like figure said to be of mixed incubus blood
findings.explanation: The English retains Merlin’s ancestry but drops Rin’s evaluative description of him as demon-like.

findings.highlight: that can cut through anything
findings.evidenceJa: 斬れない物はなく刃こぼれもしない
findings.governingReading: that can cut anything and whose blade never chips
findings.explanation: The English omits the second legendary property, the blade’s immunity to chipping.

findings.highlight: he’d yell at you for being foolish
findings.evidenceJa: 未熟者ってどやされてる
findings.governingReading: Merlin would bawl him out as an inexperienced novice.
findings.explanation: Foolish turns a rebuke of immaturity and insufficient learning into a judgment of intelligence or sense.

findings.highlight: using a great amount of magical energy
findings.evidenceJa: バカみたいに膨大な魔力を使った力技
findings.governingReading: a brute-force feat powered by Saber’s absurdly enormous magical energy
findings.explanation: The English omits both the extreme scale and Rin’s key claim that Saber’s healing looks like brute force rather than the sheath’s legendary protection.

findings.highlight: Well, if you say so…
findings.evidenceJa: 遠坂がそう言うんなら、それは正しいんだろう
findings.governingReading: If Rin says so, Shirou assumes it is probably correct.
findings.explanation: The trailing English hedge sounds doubtful and omits Shirou’s habitual confidence in Rin’s technical judgment.

findings.highlight: the sheath of Excalibur was stolen
findings.evidenceJa: 途中で敵に盗まれた
findings.governingReading: the sheath of Excalibur was stolen by an enemy partway through the legend
findings.explanation: The English drops who stole the sheath and the fact that the loss occurred partway through events.

findings.highlight: I can tell she intends to axe kick me if I laugh.
findings.evidenceJa: カカト落とし等を仕掛けてくる雰囲気がみえみえ
findings.governingReading: It is painfully obvious from her air that she is liable to launch an axe kick or something similar if he laughs.
findings.explanation: The English promotes Shirou’s comic reading of Rin’s threatening atmosphere into direct knowledge of a fixed intention and drops “or the like.”
